notes: Fiscal year ended March 31, 2026 (Toyota's 'fiscal 2026'; data.js fy 'Mar 2026'). Toyota reports under IFRS in Japanese yen, so values are billions of JPY (converted exactly from yen in millions, no FX). Financial figures are from the Form 20-F filed on SEC EDGAR on June 10, 2026 (accession 0001193125-26-264811). SEC companyfacts holds only the cover-page share count for this filing so far, so no xbrl objects are attached. OWNERSHIP: asOf March 31, 2026. largestHolders is empty on purpose. The 20-F's 5% table lists only Toyota Industries Corporation (1,192,331 thousand shares, 9.17% of outstanding voting shares; the Business Report in the May 2026 convocation notice gives 9.15% after deducting 2,761,055 thousand treasury shares). The same 20-F item then says Toyota Industries tendered those shares into Toyota's tender offer for its own shares (1,192,330,962 shares bought at 3,067 yen, about 3.65 trillion yen, March 31 to April 27, 2026) and held 1,242,720 shares (0.1%) after settlement on May 25, 2026, so listing it as a 9% holder would contradict the filing. Toyota Industries itself was taken private by a Toyota Fudosan-led group and delisted on June 1, 2026 (20-F note 36). The Business Report's top-10 register list also shows The Master Trust Bank of Japan 12.80%, Custody Bank of Japan 6.10%, Nippon Life Insurance 4.86%, State Street Bank and Trust 4.62%, JPMorgan Chase Bank 4.13%, DENSO 3.45%, The Bank of New York Mellon as depositary for ADR holders 2.73%, Toyota Fudosan 1.92% (Akio Toyoda is its chairman) and AISIN 1.33%. These are shareholders of record; trust, custody and depositary banks hold for underlying owners, and none is a 5% beneficial owner in the 20-F, so none is listed. LEADER: 24,099,025 shares at March 31, 2026, from the convocation notice; the 20-F gives 24,099 thousand as of June 2026. No percentage is stated, so pctEconomic is null (for reference only, not disclosed: about 0.18% of the 13,033,931,974 shares outstanding at March 31, 2026, and about 0.20% of the smaller post-tender count). No Toyoda family aggregate is disclosed, so relation stays 'chair'. Akio Toyoda remains Chairman of the Board (Representative Director); Kenta Kon is now President, and Koji Sato became Vice Chairman in 2026. BUYBACKS: the cash-flow line 'Reissuance (repurchase) of treasury stock' is net; the statement of changes in equity shows 'Repurchase of treasury stock (39,975)' and a separate 'Reissuance of treasury stock 1,866' (yen millions), so the cash line equals the gross repurchase. FY2026 buybacks were small because the 3.65 trillion yen tender offer settled on May 25, 2026, in fiscal 2027; it will appear in next year's cash-flow statement, as will the open-market programme of up to 1 trillion yen resolved on August 4, 2026. Dividends exclude ¥125,416 million paid to non-controlling interests. STOCK COMP: note 31(4) total of ¥2,578 million, company-wide: restricted shares and RSUs for directors and operating officers plus the new stock-grant ESOP trust for senior professional/senior management employees (220,100 points granted in FY2026; the 20-F's Item 6.E says 'No shares have been granted under the ESOP Trust'). Key-management share compensation was ¥1,993 million of the total (note 34). GEOGRAPHY: the five-region table is now in Item 5 ('Operating Performance by Geography'); the audited note 5(3) gives only Japan (10,985,614), United States (18,493,969) and Other (21,205,369). 'Other' consists of Central and South America, Oceania, Africa and the Middle East.
